description: Learn to deploy and get the most out of OpenClaw

data.label: Find the detailed version of this roadmap along with other similar roadmaps
Visit the following roadmaps to keep learning
Deploy on an isolated VPS, VM, or dedicated device, not your PC
Run OpenClaw as a non-root user
Bind the gateway to localhost, not `0.0.0.0` and secure ports 18789 and 18793
Set a strong gateway auth token before exposing any service
Enable device pairing and maintain a minimal sender allowlist
Never hardcode API keys:  use environment variables
Start in read-only mode and widen permissions deliberately
Never trust external content (emails, web pages) to prevent prompt injection
Run `openclaw security audit --deep` after every config change
Update OpenClaw regularly: many security fixes ship in patch releases
Rotate all credentials immediately if a breach is suspected

content.text: Open Claw is an open-source, self-hosted AI agent that connects your messaging apps to AI models you control. You run a single gateway process on your own machine or server, and it becomes the bridge between platforms like Telegram, WhatsApp, and Discord, and an always-available AI assistant. It's designed for developers and users who want a personal AI they can message from anywhere without giving up control of their data.

questions.title: How to get started with OpenClaw?

content.text: Getting started with OpenClaw can be daunting for a first-timer.

can feel like a lot, because it requires access to your machine, including your file system, shell, and external services like Google Calendar and email. Missing a step can leave your agent unresponsive or improperly configured, which is why getting the setup right matters. With a clean and secure setup, your phone becomes the control center, and your personalized AI agent runs tasks safely in the background on your behalf nonstop.

OpenClaw needs broad system access to work, and that same access is what makes a weak setup a target. To reduce risk, you need to understand what the OpenClaw agent can access on your system. If you don't set clear limits, the agent could end up accessing more than you bargained for. When setting it up, be careful and follow the

, as this level of control poses significant security issues. If something goes wrong due to a malicious skill, a prompt injection, or a weak setup, it can affect your system. These risks should not stop you from using OpenClaw, but rather, use them as a reason to control how you set it up. Most issues come from poor setup choices, not the tool itself.
